subject: general
question: An all-women team from the Indian Army, Navy, and Air Force has successfully returned from the country’s first-ever international open-sea sailing expedition to Seychelles in June 2025.What is the name of the indigenously-built Indian Armed Services Vessel used for this Sailing Expedition?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Triveni**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An all-women team representing the **Indian Army**, **Indian Navy**, and **Indian Air Force** scripted history by successfully completing the **first-ever international open-sea sailing expedition** to **Seychelles** in **June 2025**.
 
• The expedition was conducted on the **indigenously-built** Indian Armed Services Vessel (IASV) named **Triveni**, which is a **56-foot sailing yacht** designed for long-distance maritime voyages.
 
• The crew consisted of **12 women officers**, with **four members** selected from each of the three services, demonstrating unprecedented **inter-service synergy** and cooperation.
 
• The voyage commenced from **Kochi, Kerala**, and covered a distance of approximately **1,500 nautical miles** across the **Indian Ocean** to reach **Victoria, Seychelles**.
 
• This initiative was aimed at promoting **Nari Shakti** (Women Power) and showcasing the professional capabilities of women in the **Indian Armed Forces** in the domain of adventure and maritime navigation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Vessel Characteristics:** The **Triveni** is a testament to the **Atmanirbhar Bharat** (Self-Reliant India) initiative, as it was **indigenously designed and constructed** in India, equipped with modern navigation and communication systems for open-sea survival.
 
• **Route and Duration:** The expedition was flagged off in **May 2025** and navigated through challenging weather conditions and **monsoon winds** in the **Arabian Sea** before reaching its destination in **June 2025**.
 
• **International Relations:** The arrival of the all-women team in **Seychelles** was a significant diplomatic gesture, reinforcing the **Security and Growth for All in the Region (SAGAR)** vision promoted by the **Government of India**.
 
• **Training and Preparation:** Before the international leg, the officers underwent rigorous training at the **Indian Naval Watermanship Training Centre (INWTC)** and participated in several coastal trial runs to build endurance and technical skills.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Tri-Service Integration:** This expedition is a prime example of the **Chief of Defence Staff (CDS)** mandate to integrate the three wings of the military for joint operations and adventure activities.
 
• **Historical Context:** This mission follows the legacy of previous maritime feats like **Navika Sagar Parikrama** (the all-women circumnavigation of the globe), but it is unique for being the first **tri-service** international open-sea sailing mission.
 
• **Global Impact:** By reaching the port of **Victoria**, the team highlighted **India's maritime prowess** and its commitment to fostering gender equality within the **Defence Services** on a global stage.
 
• **Technical Skill:** The crew managed all aspects of the voyage themselves, including **navigation**, **seamanship**, and **mechanical repairs** mid-sea, proving the high standard of training provided by the **Indian Armed Forces**.
